summary: Round 8 hypotheses scan, 26 Sep ~10:40 UTC. (1) E10 and the 0.955/0.956 wave: there is still NO public source. The newest competition kernel run is Harmonic Fusion V3 (25 Sep 09:09Z); x138 has not run since 21 Sep; nothing from anvithpothula or thtennant since 24 Sep. The only new dataset is koushikrudra/biohub-zerogpu-consensus-v1: a static submission.csv plus 'text_decoder_v6.csv', not a method. LB 10:23Z: 3,924 teams, we are Rank 189 at 0.954 (silver line ~196). Counts: 0.956 27 (+1), 0.955 50 (+4). The 39 movers since 08:23Z all submitted 00:02-06:11Z, the daily pattern. P2 is not met and E10 is not triggered. (2) RED TEAM of overlap consensus. The sibling plancheck (PC8-01..12) already covers several points: the G-A FAIL, the crash/overlap error-class conflation, the MAX_S/thread timing, G-LB vs R4, and the missing K6 mode in dummy_gates. This scan adds mechanisms and tests on top. (a) The K6 kernel has hard post-writer checks: the retention guard and the final asserts require every edge to be exactly t+1. overlapcons_check only enforces forward time, so a splice bug would ERROR the whole hidden run instead of falling back. Add dt == +1 to the fail-soft invariant. (b) verify_offset has no dt+-1 exclusion. A hidden embryo with both overlaps and frozen frames (7% of 6bba frames) could register at the wrong time shift. (c) The 4 visible dummy clips do not overlap each other, so every Kaggle dummy tests only the no-op path. A --lab K6 build on the train pair 44b6_0113de3b + 44b6_c8e2a523 exercises the real notebook path, including the guards. (d) A 2-bit probe answers the decision-relevant questions in one slot: is there overlap in the PUBLIC-sized group, and in the PRIVATE group? It uses error class plus latency, and it also separates crashes from the overlap signal. (e) A finals tie rule keyed to those bits: with public-free/private-overlap, K6 must tie K2 exactly; with public overlap, a tie means the gain did not transfer, so K2 stays. (f) An honest G-B reading: the gain side is biased by the in-sample detector and the head-train stems, while the harm side transfers. The 6bba clause holds by construction (exp64 has no 6bba clips; G-A accepted 0 6bba pairs), not by measurement. (3) No closed idea is revived by a new fact.

findings.what: 2-BIT PROBE WITH CRASH SEPARATION (replaces the 1-bit G-P encoding; same single slot). Mechanism: after registration, count accepted pairs per filename prefix (embryo code). Group rule: when there are exactly 2 prefixes and the smaller holds 15-45% of the videos, S = pairs inside the smaller (public-sized) group and L = pairs inside the larger (private) group; any other structure = AMBIGUOUS. Outputs: (i) no pair, or S only with L = 0 -> valid minimal CSV -> COMPLETE -> STOP the line (overlap only in the public embryo has no private value; adopting K6 would then be public-only tuning). (ii) L = 1 and S = 0 -> deliberately malformed CSV written at once -> 'Scoring/Format Error' with latency close to the baseline. (iii) L = 1 and S = 1, or AMBIGUOUS with >= 1 pair -> the same malformed CSV, but only after time.sleep(4 h) -> 'Scoring/Format Error' with latency > baseline + 3.5 h. (iv) Probe failure inside the outer try -> no CSV -> 'CSV Not Found'. (v) Any 'Threw Exception', timeout or Kaggle Error -> UNKNOWN (crash) -> stop and ask the user. Gain: no score gain. It decides (a) whether K6 can touch private at all, which saves a 7.5 h K6 run and a slot when L = 0, and (b) which tie rule applies (R8H-2). Arithmetic: baseline probe latency = ~10k hidden frames x 0.16 s / (1-4 procs) = 410-1,600 s + ~0.3 h queue, i.e. <= ~0.8 h; the slow branch is >= 4 h. The 10-min poller separates the two easily. Runtime: <= 5 h CPU on the hidden rerun (hidden reruns do not use the GPU quota). R8: the answer arrives by ~17:00Z if submitted by ~12:00Z, before the PC8-12 K6 target of ~20:00Z.

findings.what: FINALS RULE IF K6 TIES K2 (0.954). Pre-register it before K6 scores, keyed to the R8H-1 bits. T1 (S = 0, L = 1): K6 is byte-equivalent to K2 on every public clip, and our kernels are deterministic (CONTEXT 19:05 curator (c)). So K6 public MUST equal 0.954; any other value = bug/non-determinism -> do not adopt. A tie is the expected no-harm read, and adoption rests on G-B plus G-D. Pair = {K6, twin #38}; K2 leaves. T2 (S = 1, or AMBIGUOUS): the public embryo is itself overlap-rich, so the splice ran out-of-sample there. If the lab transfers, the expected public delta is +0.002..+0.003 on a 44b6-type embryo. Adopt only at public >= 0.955, which is a real step between deterministic kernels. At a 0.954 tie keep {#37, #38}: the gain did not show where it could, and the only remaining evidence is the in-sample lab, the edge-filter pattern (+0.016 local, 0 on LB). At <= 0.953 always keep {#37, #38}. T3 (1-bit probe kept): G-LB as written adopts at a tie, but CONTEXT must say plainly that the adoption then rests on the in-sample G-B alone. Never {K6, K2}: both carry the insertion, so that pair loses the insertion hedge.

findings.what: K6 FAIL-SOFT GAP: the notebook's hard checks are stricter than the stage's invariant check. After write_test_submission, the x138 retention-guard cell raises RuntimeError on any edge whose target t != source t + 1, on negative coordinates and on non-contiguous ids; the final validator asserts the same (l.822 'bad edge time'). overlapcons_check checks only t_target > t_source, in-degree <= 1, out-degree <= 2 and finite coordinates. Any splice bug that creates a dt = 2 edge, for example a rewire through an agree node in the wrong frame, would pass the stage and then ERROR the whole K6 hidden run. The K2 graphs would not be restored, and the slot and the line are lost. Mechanism of the fix: add 'int(t_target) == int(t_source) + 1', 't >= 0' and 'rounded z/y/x >= 0' to overlapcons_check, so a violation falls back to the unspliced graphs ('OVERLAPCONS FAILED'). Gain: protects the K6 run (finals are unaffected either way). Cost: O(edges), negligible.
findings.evidence: .claude/worktrees/wf_b39793f6-e79-5/tools/build_probe_kernel.py overlapcons_check ('does not go forward in time' only); .claude/worktrees/wf_b39793f6-e79-5/experiments/exp66_k6_overlapcons/exp66-k6-overlapcons.ipynb retention guard ('_guard_node_time[_guard_target] != _guard_node_time[_guard_source] + 1' -> raise 'invalid lineage edge'; negative coordinate check) and final asserts l.814-824.
findings.action: Before the G-D dummy: extend overlapcons_check. Add a unit test in which a synthetic splice output with a dt = 2 edge and one with a negative rounded coordinate both fall back to the input graphs. Rebuild K6 (the ENABLE=0 byte-identity must still hold).

findings.what: dt-UNIQUENESS CHECK IN REGISTRATION (false time-shift guard). verify_offset accepts an offset when 3 overlap frames are >= 99.9% voxel-equal. In a clip with frozen or duplicated frames (CONTEXT A16: 7% of 6bba frames), the 3 check frames can fall inside frozen stretches. Then dt+-1 also passes, and the vote winner is not guaranteed to be the true dt. A wrong dt maps B's nodes one frame off. Every moving cell then becomes a non-agree node, the splice imports time-shifted tracks, and it harms exactly where it acts. Fix: after acceptance, also verify (dt-1, dz, dy, dx) and (dt+1, dz, dy, dx) on the same check frames, and require both to FAIL (< 99.9%). Otherwise reject the pair ('ambiguous_dt'). This only removes pairs, so it cannot add harm. Cost: 4 extra frame reads per candidate pair; G-A verify took 17.9 s for 74 candidates on the laptop, so +~25 s at most. Expected gain: 0 on train (G-A had 0 wrong offsets, and the 44b6 crops have no frozen frames); it is insurance for a hidden embryo that has both overlaps and frozen frames.

Rerun only the verify step of G-A on the 49 accepted pairs (anchors cached; ~1 min). It must still accept 49/49, which is a no-regression check, not a new gate. Build it into both the probe and K6 so the two agree.

So the standard G-D dummy exercises only the no-op path, and the writer hold, the splice, the node-id handling, the retention guard and the final asserts never run together before the hidden run. Build a --lab K6 variant with the trainlab TEST_DIR mechanism: --train-stems 44b6_0113de3b,44b6_c8e2a523,44b6_0b24845f,44b6_2f31fc2f (2 accepted pairs: 55 frames/8.8% and 51 frames/9.8%). Gate: log 'OVERLAPCONS registration ... accepted 2', 'OVERLAPCONS DONE' with spliced > 0, no FAILED/SKIPPED, the notebook COMPLETES (guards pass), and the CSV rows for those stems equal overlap_lab.py's replay of the same K2 graphs plus the splice (row digest). Gain: no score gain; it removes the 'first run on hidden' risk of the active path. Cost: ~4 clips x ~4-5 min GPU + setup, about 25-30 min, and no submission slot.

findings.what: HONEST G-B READING (write it before exp64 is read). (1) The 6bba clause 'zero changed edges' is NOT measured by exp64 (71 44b6 clips only). It holds by construction: G-A accepted 0 6bba pairs over 128 videos, so the splice is the identity there. Say so and do not report it as a lab pass. (2) Detector bias: x138's detector, the V1284 head and DaughterNet saw train clips. When both copies are in-sample the detector has memorised the same cells, so copies disagree less than they would out of sample: the GAIN magnitude is likely biased low, and so is the number of components touched. The HARM rate per spliced component (GT edges broken / fixed inside spliced components) is the part that transfers. Report fixed, broken and their ratio with a leak-group bootstrap, and compare the component count with the exp39+ef simulation (+89 FN units, 198 discordant unique edges). (3) Report the 44b6 delta also on the stems NOT used to train the x138 head (exp60 excluded 20 head stems; PC8-04 notes they are inside exp64's 71), as the least in-sample read: info only, fixed now. (4) Group concentration: report the delta without leak group 0 and the per-group signs (the design put 75% of the simulated gain in the 24-video group 0), as info. (5) No knob moves after the read: fragment_policy='rollback' was committed 10:02Z, before any exp64 number; min_gap and max_nonowner stay None. A G-B fail on magnitude with harm ~0 is a power fail and still STOPS the line (no threshold change).

findings.what: RUNTIME TRANSFER RATIO so the probe latency bounds K6's hidden stage time. The probe runs the CPU 'sparse' path in 4 spawn processes; K6 runs the GPU max_pool path in 4 threads (GIL-bound blake2b loop per anchor, a bincount threshold per frame). The probe's hidden latency therefore does not bound K6's stage directly. Measure both on the same 4 visible clips (~400 frames): the probe commit log per-frame time, and the K6 G-D dummy 'OVERLAPCONS registration ... anchors Xs' line. Then ratio r = K6_s_per_frame / probe_s_per_frame, and the bound is K6_stage_hidden <= r x (L_probe_hi - probe setup). Gate: if r x (L_probe_hi - 0.1 h) > 900 s (50% of MAX_S), set BIOHUB_OVERLAPCONS_MAX_S = 3600 before the K6 submit. That is safe: BUDGET_S 33000 + 3600 = 36,600 s = 10.2 h < 12 h, and K2 L_hi is 7.54 h. This prevents the silent 'SKIPPED (time)' outcome in which K6 equals K2, the tie is misread, and the line is lost.
findings.evidence: ga_train.json timing (0.1612 s/frame/worker, 19,900 frames, 813 s wall with 4 procs); exp65 kernel-metadata enable_gpu false and anchors_all spawn Pool; builder OVERLAPCONS_KNOBS MAX_S 1800 / BUDGET_S 33000 with ThreadPoolExecutor; #37 L in (7.36, 7.54] h; sibling PC8-03.
findings.action: Print the per-frame time in both logs (probe already logs anchors progress; add s/frame). Compute r at G-D, then bound the stage from the probe latency and choose MAX_S (1800 or 3600) by this rule, pre-registered now.

findings.what: G-A FACTS FOR THE USER'S DECISION (the numbers only; the sibling PC8-01 carries the rule). Registration is exact and false-free: 58 of the 62 GT-linked pairs produced a candidate at the exact GT offset (0 wrong offsets). 43 were accepted; 15 were rejected by the pre-registered floors (11 spatial 2.2-4.8%, 4 with 1-4 overlapping frames), and 1 more below-floor pair produced no candidate. 3 pairs above the floors produced no candidate at all (808952d6|aaf8b0ea 12 frames/25%, 996155de|aaf8b0ea 10 frames/35%, a21120c2|d78e09d9 50 frames/9%), most likely because the per-frame p99.5 anchor threshold differs between crops. The 6 extra accepted pairs have 100% voxel equality. 0 of 128 6bba videos and 0 cross-embryo pairs were accepted. Low recall costs gain, not harm. So the scientific case to continue is sound, but G-A FAILED as written: '>= 60 of 65', and splits.json holds 62 links. Continuing is a post-hoc user decision.
